question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
**Yes.** Electricity prices are rising much faster than prices overall, though the gap has narrowed in recent months.

**Latest figures (August 2026, year-on-year, original series, ABS monthly CPI):**
- **Electricity:** +13.2%
- **All groups CPI:** +4.0%

So electricity inflation is more than three times overall inflation.

**How it has changed:**
| Period | Electricity | All groups |
|---|---|---|
| Jan–Jun 2025 | −5.9% to −13.2% | 1.9%–2.4% (Apr–Jun) |
| Oct 2025 | +37.1% | 3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | +37.0% | 3.7% |
| Jun 2026 | +22.4% | 3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | +6.1% | 3.5% |
| Aug 2026 | +13.2% | 4.0% |

**Reading the numbers:**
- Electricity has outpaced overall inflation every month since July 2025. Before that, through the first half of 2025, electricity prices were falling year-on-year.
- Some of the swing probably comes from government energy bill rebates, rather than only from changes in underlying power prices. That would explain why prices appeared to fall in early 2025 and then jumped by 20–37% a year as the rebates were wound back. The data doesn't break out how much of each move is due to rebates.
- The rate peaked at about 37% (October 2025 and February 2026) and was down to 13.2% by August 2026. The drop to 6.1% in July 2026 likely happened because the big jump from July 2025 fell out of the 12-month comparison. That suggests the worst of the electricity surge is over, though it's still well ahead of the overall rate.

Electricity is also one reason overall inflation has stayed around 3.5–4.6% since late 2025, above the RBA's 2–3% target band.
